name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: US flu admissions 7x last year; severity low
summary: US flu admissions hit 9,584 in the week to 7 Nov, over seven times a year earlier; CDC still rates severity low
state: CDC reported 9,584 flu hospital admissions in the week to 7 Nov, with seven jurisdictions at high or very high activity, up from two a week earlier, and in-season severity still rated low; it estimates at least 36,000 hospitalisations and 2,100 deaths so far, including five children (CDC). Most cases are an H1N1 strain with mutations, and activity began in the South and West (KPTV, citing AP, 14 Nov). Searches on 19 Nov found no new WHO variant designation and no health systems reported as strained, so an unusually early US season keeps Watch.
for_you: UKHSA and the NHS set out who is eligible for a free flu vaccine this winter. Older people, young children, pregnant women and those with long-term conditions are most at risk of severe illness.
rubric_hit: Watch: unusually early flu season (US admissions 9,584 in week to 7 Nov, over 7x a year earlier); no health system strain or VOC for Alert

sources.title: CDC — Weekly US Influenza Surveillance Report, week 44, ending 7 Nov 2026
KPTV (AP) — Flu season is off to a very early start; here's where cases are surging

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
